findings.title: validator-dispatch fires at 73% frequency with zero observable output — A5 finding from opus chain
findings.note: NEW FINDING (elevated from opus chain iter-013 A5 finding). The iter-013 analysis found validator-dispatch at 145/200 traces (73%), with per-invocation duration 45598ms. Task breakdown: discover_validators (5ms), select_validator_per_shape (5194ms LLM), dispatch_validators (0ms — does not actually dispatch), propagate_failure_mode (2668ms LLM), learning_signal_write (0ms — writes nothing). The dispatch_validators task completes in 0ms and 'actually_dispatches: false'. The propagate_failure_mode task writes 0 output impulses. The parent trace's failure_mode field remains null when the child execution fails without throwing (engine.ts catch block misses non-throw failures). This means the substrate's dominant LLM budget (73% of all executions, ~45 seconds each) is spent on a lifecycle template that selects validators that never dispatch and writes learning signals that never write. This is not a trace-accuracy issue — it is a functional correctness failure. Evidence is from untracked investigation files; direct verification command against live traces would require a trace query tool. The claim is consistent with the coverage regression (if the most common template produces nothing, reachable_learned cannot grow).
